transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer security, my name is Yasmin. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Yasmin. I received a very urgent email this morning that looks like it's from S-Net saying my broadband account has been suspended due to an unpaid bill and asking me to click a link to update my payment details. I'm worried it might be a scam.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand how concerning it is to receive an urgent email threatening account suspension and requesting banking credentials. Let me inspect your billing file and review the email security headers immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Yasmin. It looked quite authentic with your company logo, but the sender address looked slightly suspicious.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we access your customer security file, could you please confirm your full installation address and your four-digit security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 41 Victoria Road, Chester, CH1 3TF, and my account PIN is 9152.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details. I have your customer account open on our central security console.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what has occurred: you received an unsolicited email purportedly from S-Net claiming your broadband service is suspended for non-payment and directing you to click an external link to submit payment details, and you want to verify whether this is genuine S-Net correspondence or a phishing fraud attempt. Have I understood correctly?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, spot on. I didn't click the link because my direct debit went through fine last week.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: First, let's verify your true account standing on our billing ledger.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does my actual balance show on your system?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your account balance is exactly zero pounds with zero outstanding charges, and your monthly direct debit collected successfully six days ago.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So my broadband account was never suspended or in arrears at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your service is completely active with zero billing restrictions.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That confirms the email message is completely fraudulent.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's examine the technical sender details of that suspicious email.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What information from the email do you need?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What is the exact display name and the email address shown inside the angle brackets in the From header?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The display name says 'S-Net Billing Support', but the actual email address is support@snet-billing-update-uk.com.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That domain is an illegitimate third-party domain and has no connection with S-Net.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: All genuine S-Net emails come from @s-net.co.uk, right?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, all official correspondence originates strictly from @s-net.co.uk or @notifications.s-net.co.uk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What does the link in the email point to if I hover my mouse over it?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you hover your mouse cursor over the payment button without clicking, what URL appears in your browser status bar?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It points to a weird web address: https://secure-login-portal-verify.net/snet/login.php.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That URL is a known credential harvesting phishing site designed to steal S-Net portal logins and debit card numbers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am so glad I had the sense not to click on it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You did exactly the right thing by checking your actual account status before interacting with the email.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you report that domain to your cybersecurity team so other customers are protected?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check our threat intelligence database to submit a domain takedown request.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello? Are you still on the line with me?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I am right here, apologies for the pause while our threat response portal was loading the domain records.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's fine, I just wanted to be sure the call didn't drop.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our security operations center has logged snet-billing-update-uk.com and submitted an emergency DNS takedown notice to the domain registrar.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does that block the website for everyone on the internet?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the registrar will revoke the authoritative nameservers, and our S-Net Web Safe filter will block the IP address across all customer broadband connections within fifteen minutes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is brilliant that you can block it network-wide so quickly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you entered your S-Net username, password, or banking card details on any unfamiliar websites recently?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I haven't entered my password anywhere, and I never clicked any links.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms your credentials and banking details have not been compromised.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I change my S-Net account password anyway just to be on the safe side?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Changing your password as a proactive measure is always excellent security hygiene.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will log into the official My S-Net portal and update my password to a strong new phrase.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Would you like me to enable two-factor authentication on your account so every login requires an SMS code?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes please! Having two-factor authentication will stop anyone logging in even if they ever got my password.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me update the multi-factor authentication policy on your customer profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are you still updating the two-factor setting on your screen?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, still here, two-factor SMS verification has just successfully locked onto your account profile.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, excellent.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: From now on, whenever anyone attempts to sign into your online account, a one-time six-digit passcode will be dispatched to your registered mobile number.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That provides ironclad protection against unauthorized access.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does S-Net offer an email security scanner for our home inbox?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, our mail gateways scan all incoming email traffic for SPF, DKIM, and DMARC alignment before delivery to your inbox.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How did this email bypass the gateway filter then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The attackers used a freshly registered domain that had not yet accumulated negative sender reputation scores.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That explains why it slipped through into my main inbox folder.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How do cybercriminals manage to create emails that look so identical to official S-Net templates?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Phishing attackers scrape official CSS stylesheets and logo image assets directly from public web pages to craft convincing lookalike templates.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That explains why the fonts, color scheme, and logos looked indistinguishable from real bills.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Always check the actual sending address and never click embedded authentication links inside unprompted emails.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll make sure to always log in directly through my own browser bookmarks in the future.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Should I forward this email to the national reporting center as well?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can also forward the message to the National Cyber Security Centre at report@phishing.gov.uk.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I will forward a copy to the NCSC reporting inbox right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And please forward the email as an attachment to phishing@s-net.co.uk so our automated security parser can extract technical routing headers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Forwarding it right now to phishing@s-net.co.uk... sent! And now deleting it completely from my inbox and trash folder.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That permanently removes the malicious link from your email client.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You've been incredibly helpful today. You verified my zero balance, confirmed the phishing scam, submitted the takedown, and enabled two-factor authentication.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It was my absolute pleasure assisting you. Is there anything else regarding your account security or broadband that I can check today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, everything is completely secure and protected now. Thank you so much!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today. Stay safe online and have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Yasmin, goodbye.
